H1: Evac+Chair iEvac Smoke Hood and Fire Escape Hood – EBP-900
Current H1: Evac+Chair EBP-900 iEvac Smoke - Fire Escape Hood
Subtitle: ASTM E2952 Certified Fire Escape Hood That Protects Against Smoke, Carbon Monoxide, and Toxic Gases During a Building Evacuation
Current subtitle: Evac+Chair EBP-900
Revised Product Description
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
The Evac+Chair iEvac Smoke/Fire Hood is a fire escape hood that gives a person filtered air to breathe while they get out of a building on fire. It protects against smoke and by-products of combustion, including carbon monoxide and hydrogen cyanide, as well as other toxic gases, chemical and biological agents, and fine particles.
The iEvac is certified to ASTM E2952, the American standard for air-purifying smoke escape devices. This smoke escape hood comes vacuum-sealed in a small foil bag, can be put on in under 30 seconds, and comes in one universal size that works with eyeglasses, beards, and long hair. It is maintenance-free, needs no fit test, and has a shelf life of 5½ years from the date of manufacture.
Certification: Certified by the Safety Equipment Institute (SEI) to ASTM E2952, the American standard for air-purifying respiratory protective smoke escape devices
Designation: Qualified Anti-Terrorism Technology, U.S. Department of Homeland Security
Gases: Protects against carbon monoxide, hydrogen cyanide, hydrogen sulfide, chlorine, ammonia, sulfur dioxide, formaldehyde, and other toxic gases
Particles: HEPA filter removes soot, fumes, aerosols, and sub-micron particles, including radioactive particles
Heat: Clear hood material withstands radiant heat up to 1700°F (927°C) at 9½”
Filters: Twin filters for easier breathing and a wider field of view
Hood: Clear hood with high-visibility reflective strips and a silicone neck dam; protects the lungs, head, eyes, and face
Fit: One universal size; works with eyeglasses, beards, and long hair; latex-free; no fit test required
Donning: Can be put on in under 30 seconds
Packaging: Vacuum-sealed in a puncture-proof, waterproof foil laminate bag, 5½”W×4¾”D×5½”H
Weight: 1.4 lbs, ready to use
Shelf Life: 5½ years from date of manufacture; maintenance-free
Use: One-time use only
Available Models and Options
EBP-900 – iEvac Smoke/Fire Hood: Single fire escape hood, vacuum-sealed in a foil bag
[H2] Where to Keep a Smoke Hood
Keep the iEvac where people may have to escape through smoke: at desks and workstations, near exits, or beside an evacuation chair in a stairwell, so it is ready the moment a fire alarm sounds.
Typical applications include:
Offices, corporate buildings, and high-rise buildings
Hospitals, senior living, and care facilities
Government buildings and correctional facilities
Hotels, sporting arenas, and mass transit
Homes
Explore Anchortex's Evacuation Chairs and Stretchers collection for more evacuation equipment.
[H2] Frequently Asked Questions
What is a fire escape hood?
A fire escape hood, also called a smoke hood or emergency escape hood, is a clear hood with filters that a person pulls over their head to breathe filtered air while escaping a fire. It is for escape only, not for fighting a fire or going back into a building.
How long does the iEvac protect?
ASTM E2952 requires at least 15 minutes of protection against each test gas. In that testing, the iEvac protected against carbon monoxide for more than 45 minutes at 3,000 ppm and against hydrogen cyanide for more than 90 minutes at 400 ppm.
Can the iEvac be used more than once?
No. It is for one-time use only. An unused hood has a shelf life of 5½ years from the date of manufacture.
Can people with glasses or beards wear it?
Yes. It comes in one universal size and can be worn with eyeglasses, beards, and long hair, and no fit test is needed.
[H2] About Evac+Chair Evacuation Chairs
Evac+Chair makes stair evacuation chairs, powered stair chairs, evacuation sleds, and accessories for moving people with limited mobility on stairs, in an emergency or every day.
The Evac+Chair line includes:
Emergency evacuation chairs: The 300H, 400H, 600H, and 750H stair evacuation chairs for controlled travel down the stairs
Powered stair climbing chairs: The battery powered Power 800 and Power 900 for going up and down the stairs
Stair transport seat: The IBEX 700H Tran-Seat for two-person transport up and down the stairs
Evacuation sleds and mats: The Evac+Sled, Ulti-Mat, and Evac+Sheet rescue sheet
Accessories: Comfy Seat, transfer seat, storage cabinets, anti-theft alarms, and the iEvac smoke and fire escape hood
[H2] About Evac+Chair
Evac+Chair has made stairway evacuation chairs since 1982, and its chairs were designed in the United States. Explore the full line of Evac+Chair evacuation chairs at Anchortex.

Notes and Questions
Keywords: as Ricky asked, I checked the results page for "smoke hood" (400). It mixes escape hoods with kitchen, grill, and stove hoods and patents, while the "fire escape hood" results are all escape products. So "fire escape hood" stays the primary keyword (H1, subtitle, first sentence, an FAQ, the meta title, and the meta description), and "smoke hood" is in the H1, a subhead, and an FAQ. "Smoke escape hood" is in the second intro paragraph, "emergency escape hood" in an FAQ, and the product name "Smoke/Fire Hood" covers "fire smoke hood."
Manufacturer: the iEvac is made by Elmridge Protection Products (Boca Raton, FL), and Evac+Chair resells it. The Evac+Chair page has one sentence, so the specs come from the Elmridge web page and the Elmridge EBP-900 data sheet. I kept "Evac+Chair" first in the H1 because it is our vendor for this product. Would you prefer "iEvac" or Elmridge first?
Model: Elmridge now calls this hood the "iEvac E900" (item E900). The data sheet uses EBP-900, like our page, so I kept EBP-900.
Left out: "the only U.S. certified smoke hood" (our current copy; Elmridge and SEI say it is the only hood certified to ASTM E2952, but it is a comparison claim), and the data sheet's list of ebola, anthrax, ricin, smallpox, sarin, and tear gas, to keep the copy about fire escape.
Price: Elmridge sells the E900 on its own website for $250. Ours is $319 with compare-at $425 (75%). No change made.
Images: our one image (1214×783) has a "WATCH VIDEO" badge in the corner (it is the Evac+Chair video thumbnail), but there is no video on our page. Elmridge has larger photos: a side view (1944×2592), two people going down a smoky office stairwell (1944×2592), and a features diagram (3000×2000). Would you like me to add them as "Evac-Chair-iEvac-EBP-900-Fire-Escape-Hood-Side-View.jpg", "Evac-Chair-iEvac-EBP-900-Fire-Escape-Hood-Stairwell-View.jpg", and "Evac-Chair-iEvac-EBP-900-Fire-Escape-Hood-Features-Diagram.jpg", and replace the current one?
Accessories: Elmridge also sells a demo hood, carry pouch, wall rack, and wall cabinet for the iEvac. We do not sell them, so they are not mentioned.
Weight: the variant is set to 5 lbs; the hood weighs 1.4 lbs ready to use. Is 5 lbs the shipping weight?
Duplicate content: our current description repeats the Evac+Chair sentence twice, plus an old "About Evac+Chair of North America" paragraph ending "Ask about their lifetime warranty." The hood has a 5½-year shelf life and no warranty is published, so I left the warranty out. The new copy is fully rewritten.
Current meta description is the general GSA pricing line. GSA is not mentioned in the description, per your note on the other tabs.
